origin: Single motivated bug-fix from v2, per Researcher review (strategies/day_trading/nfp_fade/v2/review.md, 2026-09-23). Reviewing v2's in-sample results required diffing v1 vs v2 trade-by-trade journals per pair to isolate what the calendar-completeness fix actually changed. That diff surfaced a SECOND, distinct defect beyond the one v2 already fixed: the three per-symbol hardcoded NFP-date tables (one independently typed per EA instance, per one_ea_per_symbol_chart) are NOT consistent with each other, and at least two of their entries contradict v1's own already-validated ground truth. Specifically: GBPUSD.r's v2 table is missing 2022.02.04 (present in both EUR's and JPY's v2 tables, and explicitly confirmed as a real BLS release date in v1/review.md Part 1's cross-check); USDJPY's v2 table is missing 2022.04.01 (a date only JPY's v1 sample ever had, but which v1/review.md Part 1 explicitly named as real -- 'March 2022's 431k report'). Since there is exactly one real BLS calendar, three independently-typed per-symbol tables that disagree with each other cannot all be right -- this is transcription drift, not a signal question, and is the exact risk EA Coder's own v2 coded-status note flagged as unverified ('the remaining ~100 non-exception entries... were not each individually fact-checked one by one'). This is the ONLY change in v3: everything else (measurement window, threshold, SL/TP, hold time, sizing, pairs, safety rules) is byte-for-byte identical to v2, per this project's house rule against bundling multiple changes into one refinement.
thesis: Unchanged from v1/v2 -- see v1/spec.json for the full thesis writeup (Street Smarts / Raschke & Connors 1996 'News Strategy' fading the initial overreaction to a scheduled 8:30am ET release, applied to NFP specifically).

calendar_trigger.rule: unchanged mechanism from v2 -- actual historical BLS Employment Situation (NFP) release date, from a hardcoded per-month lookup table, NOT computed from a day-of-month rule, NOT MT5's CalendarValueHistory() API.
calendar_trigger.change_reasoning: v2's table content had a demonstrated defect: at least 2 of the ~324 pair-month entries (108 dates x 3 symbols) contradicted v1's own already-validated ground truth, and the 3 per-symbol tables are not identical to each other despite representing the same single real-world calendar event. This is a data-integrity fix, not a rule-design change.
calendar_trigger.implementation: SINGLE canonical table of 108 NFP release dates (2017.01-2025.12), used identically by all three EA instances -- no longer three independently-typed copies. Recommend EA Coder implement this as one shared #include file included by all three symbol EAs (EURUSD.r/GBPUSD.r/USDJPY), so future edits can never again silently diverge per-symbol the way v2's did. If a shared #include is impractical given the existing per-symbol EA structure, at minimum EA Coder must generate the three tables from one script/source list and diff them byte-for-byte before compiling any of the three, reporting the diff explicitly (must be empty).
calendar_trigger.required_corrections_confirmed: Restore 2022.02.04 to GBPUSD.r's table (present in v2's EUR and JPY tables, was in v1's GBP sample too, dropped only from v2 GBP). Restore 2022.04.01 to USDJPY's table (was in v1's JPY sample, explicitly confirmed real by v1/review.md Part 1, dropped from v2 JPY).
calendar_trigger.verification_requirement: Before handing to Backtester: (1) confirm all three symbol tables are byte-identical (108 entries each, same dates); (2) confirm both January exceptions from v2 are still present (2020.01.10, 2021.01.08) plus the two 2025 exceptions EA Coder flagged as moderate-confidence in v2's coded note (2025.01.10, 2025.07.03) -- re-verify these four against a live source if browse/internet access is available in this session, since v2's coding session explicitly did not have it; (3) spot-check at least 10 more dates spanning 2023-2025 (the still-entirely-unchecked out-of-sample window) against a real BLS schedule source, since that window will be used for the one-shot OOS validation once this version is locked.
calendar_trigger.fallback_if_month_missing_from_table: unchanged from v2 -- if a month is genuinely missing (should not happen for 2017-2025), skip that month's trade entirely, do not fall back to any computed rule.

entry: unchanged from v1/v2 -- see v1/spec.json for measurement_window (T+0 to T+10min), MinSpikeSizePipsFloor=15, MinSpikeVsAvgMultiplier=1.2, SpikeHistoryWindowEvents=12, MinHistoryToAdapt=6, skip_conditions. Do not modify any of these values.
exit: unchanged -- 60-minute hold backstop after the measurement window closes, end_of_day_flat_hour_server=22.
safety_rules: unchanged -- see v1/spec.json (consecutive_loss_pause threshold=6, daily_loss_stop_percent=5.0, max_drawdown_stop_percent=15.0, never_scale_up_after_loss, max_one_position_per_pair_per_event, live_account_opt_in_required).
tunable_parameters_to_sweep: none for v3, same as v1/v2 -- this is a data-correctness fix, not a parameter search.

demo_criteria.rationale: unchanged from v1/v2 -- low-frequency calendar-event strategy, min_days is the binding constraint, not trade count. Not adjusted despite v1/v2's thin trade counts, per house rule against moving the bar after seeing results.

expected_outcome_note: This is a data-integrity fix on top of v2's already-correct completeness fix, not a signal redesign. Expect trade count to move by at most a couple trades per pair (restoring 2 known-dropped dates, GBP +1 / JPY +1 relative to v2) plus whatever the fuller verification pass turns up if other silent drops are found during the required byte-diff check. Do not expect this to resolve v1/v2's core open question (GBP/JPY/EUR all still within noise range on a ~67-70 trade combined sample) -- its purpose is solely to make the config trustworthy enough to spend the one-shot out-of-sample check on. Once this version's three tables are confirmed byte-identical and re-backtested clean on the same in-sample range, out-of-sample validation (2023.01.01-2025.12.31) is the next step, not another mechanism tweak.
